learn.overlap.adjust.title: The plan and the budget are adjusted to match
learn.overlap.adjust.body: While offices finish their plans, the budget office is already fitting them to the money the {lgu} expects to collect. Cuts in one change the other, back and forth, until they agree. For the {fy} budget the {lgu} finished both in October {prev}.
learn.overlap.review.title: Spending starts while the national check runs
learn.overlap.review.body: The {lgu} can spend from January. The national government’s review of the budget happens in the same months, and can still strike out an item that breaks the rules.
learn.overlap.report.title: Spending and reporting run together
learn.overlap.report.body: Offices report what they have spent through the year, not only at the end. The final audit comes after the year closes.
learn.hero.title: How {shortName}’s budget is made
learn.hero.body: One year’s budget takes almost two years to make and account for: from the first conversation about what the {lgu} needs to the final audit of what was spent. It passes through {count} stages, and some happen at the same time. Choose any stage to see what happens, who is involved, and where you can take part.
learn.s1.title: The {fy} budget, from start to finish.
learn.s2.title: The stages are not a straight line.
learn.s2.lede: The textbook order is plan first, then budget. In practice several stages overlap, and each overlap is a moment when a figure can still move.
learn.s3.title: While one budget is being spent, the next one is being made.
learn.s3.lede: So at any moment the {lgu} is in two places in the cycle.
learn.s3.aria: Timeline: the {prev} budget is spent in {prev} while the {fy} budget is made; the {fy} budget is spent in {fy} while the {next} budget is made.

aipvs.meta.title: AIP vs Annual Budget | Learn | {siteName}
aipvs.meta.description: The difference between {shortName}'s Annual Investment Program and its Annual Budget: when each exists, why their numbers differ, and what a budget figure does and does not mean.
aipvs.move.3: Offices’ requests are cut to fit the income the {lgu} expects. This is where most AIP amounts change.
aipvs.move.5: The {lguAdj} council can question and cut items before it votes.
aipvs.move.6: The {Mayor} can veto particular items. The council can override a veto with a two-thirds vote.
aipvs.move.7: The national budget department can declare items that break the rules without effect.
aipvs.move.8: During the year, a supplemental budget, itself an ordinance, can add to or change the budget.
aipvs.hero.title: A plan and a law are not the same number.
aipvs.hero.body: This site publishes two documents from opposite ends of the {cycle}. The Annual Investment Program is what the {lgu} plans; the Annual Budget is what it may spend. This page explains the difference, why their figures differ, and what a figure on this site does and does not mean.
aipvs.s1.title: One is a request. The other is permission.
aipvs.plan.title: Annual Investment Program
aipvs.plan.body: What the {lgu}’s offices {propose} to do next year, and what they think it will cost. It is assembled office by office over months, so it is incomplete while it is being written, and nothing may be spent on the strength of it.
aipvs.law.title: Annual Budget
aipvs.law.body: The budget once the plan has been fitted to the {lgu}’s expected income, passed by the Sanggunian, and signed by the {Mayor}. It is settled, and it is permission to spend. Comparing one to the other compares a request to an outcome.
aipvs.s1.foot: On this site a year sits under {aip} while its budget is being prepared, and moves to {annual} once it is enacted.
aipvs.s2.title: Five points where an amount can move.
aipvs.s2.lede: Between the plan and the money actually spent, an amount can change at these stages of the cycle. Each links to the stage on the cycle page.
aipvs.s3.title: A budget line is permission. Spending is four steps later.
aipvs.s3.lede: This is the most common way to misread the whole site. An appropriation authorizes an amount; it does not record that the money went anywhere.
entry.meta.title: Reading an entry | Learn | {siteName}
entry.meta.description: How to read a line in {placeName}’s budget: programs, projects and activities, where the money sits, and what the reference code means.
entry.hero.title: What a line in the budget tells you.
entry.hero.body: Every entry on this site has the same parts: what kind of entry it is, how much it carries, who is responsible for it, and a reference code. This page explains each, using the shapes you will meet in {browse}.
entry.s1.title: Entries nest, and an amount is never counted twice.
entry.s1.p1: Budget entries nest. A {program} is a group of related work, say, running the {lgu}’s health centers. Inside it can sit {projects}, which have an end, and {activities}, which are ongoing.
entry.s1.p2: A program’s amount is either stated on the program itself or, when it lists projects and activities, the sum of theirs. Many programs state their own amount and list nothing beneath it. When a program does list entries, the money is recorded on them: if a program and the single entry inside it show the same amount, that is one amount described twice, not two.
entry.s1.p3: Each entry also names the {office} accountable for it, one of the eight {finishLines} it works toward, and the {fund} the money comes from.
entry.s2.title: Every entry carries a code. It is a description, not a serial number.
entry.s2.lede: You will see something like {code} beside entries in {browse}. Each group of digits says where the entry sits: the sector, the office, the section of the book, and its position inside it.
code.sector.label: Sector
code.sector.meaning: Which national spending sector the work belongs to. 8000 is Other Economic Services.
code.level.label: Level
code.level.meaning: The level of government: 1 for a province, 2 for a city, 3 for a municipality.
code.officeType.label: Office type
code.officeType.meaning: Whether the office is mandatory (01), optional (02) or other (03) under the DBM manual.
code.office.label: Office
code.office.meaning: The office's own number in the {lgu}'s coding sheet. 58 is the Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering Department.
code.section.label: Section
code.section.meaning: Which section of the budget book it prints under: 001 General Administrative Services, 002 Support to Operations, 003 Operations.
code.program.label: Program
code.program.meaning: The program's position within that section. Counting restarts in each section.
code.entry.label: Entry
code.entry.meaning: Which project or activity inside the program. 000 means the row is the program itself.
code.caption: The AIP reference code 8000-2-03-58-002-001-000 broken into its seven segments, each explained in the list below.
code.not: Two things the code does {not} do. It does not add up — a program’s code is a label, not a total of the entries beneath it. And it carries no year, so the same code is issued again for the next budget.
money.appropriation.what: The ordinance authorizes an amount for a purpose. Permission to spend.
money.allotment.what: The office is released the authority to start committing that money.
money.obligation.what: A contract is signed or a payroll run. The {lgu} is now bound to pay.
money.disbursement.what: Cash actually leaves the treasury. Only now has money been spent.
money.caption: Every figure on this site is step one. Whether the money was committed or actually paid is answered in the {lgu}’s accountability reports, not here.
ppa.programNote: Its amount is the sum of the entries below
ppa.caption: So if a program and the one entry inside it show the same amount, that is one amount described at two levels — not two amounts. Many programs list no projects or activities at all; they state their own amount instead.

glossary.hero.title: {count} terms the documents assume you know.
glossary.hero.body: Only terms you will actually meet on this site. Each is a plain-language paraphrase; for anything you intend to cite, use the official document.
glossary.footer: Definitions are paraphrased from the {bom}, the {lgc}, the {procurement}, and {lgu}. Spot something wrong? Every entry on this site takes feedback.
glossary.termsNote: Budget terms are kept in English, as they appear in the {lgu}’s documents.

aipov.meta.description: What {place}'s draft Annual Investment Program contains so far — the programs published, by which offices, and what they are meant to achieve.
aipov.meta.title: Overview | Annual Investment Program {year} | {place}
aipov.plan.lede1: The Annual Investment Program is what the {lgu}’s offices propose to do next year. Each office prepares its own and publishes when it is ready, so this page fills up over months — and until it is full, the figures below describe {published}, not what the {lgu} will spend.
aipov.plan.lede2: It becomes the Annual Budget only after the Sanggunian enacts it. The last one that did is {link}.
aipov.stat.proposed: estimated so far for FY {fy} — the cost of planned programs, not a budget
aipov.stat.offices: {lguAdj} offices have published. {left} still to come, and every one of them will move these figures.
aipov.truncated: This cycle holds more programmes than one request returns, so every figure on this page is a partial sum. The {browse} page is authoritative.
aipov.fl.all: All {total} {goals} have something proposed against them.
aipov.fl.some.one: {count} {goal} has anything proposed against it yet.
aipov.fl.some.other: {count} {goals} have anything proposed against it yet.
aipov.fl.lede: Every programme is filed against one of the {lgu}’s {link}. A {goal} with nothing beside it does not mean the {lgu} has stopped working on it — it means the offices that own it have not published their plans yet.
aipov.fl.caption: Estimated cost by {goal}, Annual Investment Program {fy}
aipov.who.one: One office, {office}, accounts for {share} of everything published so far.
aipov.who.many: {count} offices have put forward a plan.
aipov.who.lede: Offices are grouped into clusters that share a {goal}. Early in the cycle these totals say more about who has finished their paperwork than about the {lgu}’s priorities.
aipov.who.clusterCaption: Estimated cost by cluster, Annual Investment Program {fy}
aipov.who.officeCaption: Estimated cost by implementing office, Annual Investment Program {fy}
aipov.buys.none: No office has broken its plan down by kind of spending yet.
aipov.buys.claim: Of what has been costed, {share} builds something that lasts.
aipov.buys.lede: Every peso is one of three kinds: paying people, running services, or buying something that outlives the year.
aipov.buys.partial: {n} of {total} published programmes have been broken down this far; the rest carry a single figure with no split.
aipov.buys.caption: Estimated cost by expense class, Annual Investment Program {fy}
aipov.buys.empty: The breakdown appears here as offices cost their plans out. Until then each programme carries only a single estimated figure.
expense.mooeGloss: the cost of running services day to day
expense.feGloss: bank charges, interest and other financial costs
expense.coGloss: buildings, equipment and other lasting assets
aipov.fund.claim: Most of it is meant to come from the {fund}.
aipov.fund.none: No fund has been named against these plans yet.
aipov.fund.lede: A {lgu} draws on more than one purse — the general fund, the school fund, the disaster fund, money from national agencies. Each entry names the funds it draws on but not how much comes from each, so an entry naming several is counted once and shown separately rather than split.
aipov.fund.caption: Estimated cost by fund source, Annual Investment Program {fy}
entries.heading: Entries
aipov.vs.above: The estimated cost so far is above the whole {prior} budget, by {pct}.
aipov.vs.below: The estimated cost so far is below the whole {prior} budget, by {pct}.
aipov.vs.lede: A plan and a law are not the same kind of number, so read this as a direction of travel rather than a verdict — and note that {n} of {total} offices have published, so the plan is not finished. {link} is on this site in full.
aipov.vs.caption: Estimated {fy} against enacted {prior}
aipov.vs.proposedSub: so far, and still being written

annov.meta.description: Where {place}'s enacted Annual Budget goes — by purpose, by office, by expense class and by fund.
annov.meta.title: Overview | Annual Budget {year} | {place}
annov.law.rest: The budget the Sanggunian enacted for {fy}, in full.
annov.law.lede1: Every figure on this page is settled. This is not a proposal or a forecast — it is the appropriation ordinance the {lguAdj} council passed, recorded here exactly as the printed book states it, down to the centavo.
annov.law.lede2: An appropriation is permission to spend, not spending. What was actually paid out is a separate question, answered in the {lgu}’s own accountability reports rather than here.
annov.law.next: The plan for next year is {link}, still being written.
annov.stat.stated: enacted for FY {fy}: {office} for {lguAdj} offices and {special} in special purpose appropriations
annov.stat.statedBy: enacted for FY {fy} by {source}: {office} for {lguAdj} offices and {special} in special purpose appropriations
annov.stat.entries: programmes, projects and activities, across {count} {lguAdj} offices
annov.stat.capital: goes to capital outlay — buildings, equipment, anything that outlives the year
annov.for.claim: {share} of it is aimed at one {goal}: {line}.
annov.for.none: What the budget is aimed at.
annov.for.lede: Each entry is filed against one of the {lgu}’s {link}. The enacted book does not state a {goal} itself, so these are assigned from the office that implements each entry — a good guide to intent, not a claim the ordinance makes.
annov.for.caption: Enacted amount by {goal}, Annual Budget {fy}
annov.who.three: Three offices spend {share} of it between them.
annov.who.largest: The largest is {office}, at {amount}. Offices are grouped into clusters that share a {goal}.
annov.who.lede: A large budget is not the same as a large staff or a large mandate — hospitals and public works carry costs that an advisory office never will.
annov.who.clusterCaption: Enacted amount by cluster, Annual Budget {fy}
annov.who.officeCaption: Enacted amount by implementing office, Annual Budget {fy}
annov.sec.lede1: Every appropriation sits in one of three sections of the printed book. {ops} is the service an office exists to deliver. {sto} is what makes that possible from behind — records, vehicles, IT. {gas} is the cost of the office itself: its people, its premises, its running costs.
annov.sec.lede2: Most offices file nearly everything under the third, which is why it dominates. Read it as a fact about how the book is organised rather than as a measure of how much the {lgu} spends on administration.
annov.sec.caption: Enacted amount by section of the book, Annual Budget {fy}
annov.buys.claim: Almost none of this builds anything — {share} is capital outlay.
annov.buys.lede: A {lguAdj} budget is mostly people and the cost of keeping services running. That is not a criticism: salaries are how a health office delivers health. But it does mean a year’s budget builds far less than its size suggests, and that new construction is a small slice competing with everything else.
annov.buys.caption: Enacted amount by expense class, Annual Budget {fy}
annov.buys.empty: No expense-class breakdown was recorded for this year.
annov.fund.claim: Most of it comes from the {fund}.
annov.fund.lede: A {lgu} draws on more than one purse — the general fund, the school fund, the disaster fund, money from national agencies.
section.lepTag: Local Expenditure Program: the budget the {Mayor} proposed. The {lgu} has not yet posted the enacted ordinance for this year, so these figures are what was proposed, not what was appropriated.
annov.fund.special: Some funds come with rules set by law. Read what each pays for:
annov.fund.caption: Enacted amount by fund source, Annual Budget {fy}
ppmpov.meta.description: What {placeName}'s offices plan to buy this year — how much, what kind, how it will be bought, when, and by whom — from their published procurement plans.
ppmpov.meta.title: Overview | Project Procurement Management Plan {year} | {placeName}
ppmpov.mode.SMALL_VALUE_PROCUREMENT: smaller purchases, by price quotation instead of bidding
ppmpov.mode.COMPETITIVE_BIDDING: open, public bidding — the default the law expects

ppmpov.lede1: A Project Procurement Management Plan lists what one office means to buy in a year — each item, how many, at what cost, and when — so the purchase can be checked against the budget that pays for it. Offices publish their plans one at a time, so {published}, not everything the {lgu} will buy.
ppmpov.published: the figures here cover what has been published
ppmpov.lede2: The money itself is set by {link}.
ppmpov.stat.planned: planned so far for FY {fy} — a running total, not the {lgu}’s whole plan
ppmpov.type.none: No office has said what kind of purchase its items are yet.
ppmpov.type.lede: Every item is one of four kinds: goods the {lgu} takes delivery of, services someone performs, consultants’ expertise, or infrastructure that gets built.
ppmpov.type.caption: Planned amount by type of purchase, PPMP {fy}
items.heading: Items
ppmpov.how.claim: {share} of it is planned for open, competitive bidding.
ppmpov.how.none: No office has said how it will buy yet.
ppmpov.how.lede: Public bidding is the rule; the other modes are exceptions the law allows for small purchases, urgent or specialized needs. The share that goes to bidding is worth watching.

ppmpov.when.claim: The biggest month for starting purchases is {month}.
ppmpov.when.none: No purchase has a start month yet.

ppmpov.who.one: One office, {office}, plans {share} of everything published so far.

explore.lint.empty: every value is zero, so there is nothing to draw.
explore.lint.tooManyCategories: too many categories to read as a chart. Set Top N to group the rest as Other.
explore.lint.tooManySeries: more than eight series would repeat colours. Remove a breakdown or filter.
explore.lint.mixedUnits: the amounts are in different units and cannot share one axis.
explore.lint.ratioStacked: percentages of different wholes do not add up, so they cannot be stacked.
explore.lint.negativeArea: a negative amount has no size in a part-to-whole chart.
explore.lint.rankAsLength: a rank is a position, not an amount, so it is not drawn as a length.
explore.lint.lineUnordered: a line joins values in order, and this breakdown has no order. Try a bar.
explore.lint.onePoint: one value is not a trend. Pick more years.
explore.lint.fewPoints: a scatter needs at least three points.
explore.lint.heatmapThin: a heat map needs at least two rows and two columns.
explore.lint.kpiMany: more than twelve big numbers read better as a table.
explore.lint.otherDominates: Other is bigger than everything shown. Raise Top N.
explore.lint.mapTotals: a map of totals mostly shows where people live. Choose Per resident.
explore.guide.starter.places.name: Where in the {lgu} the FY{year} AIP goes
explore.guide.starter.places.blurb: The plan's projects and activities by barangay, per resident (PSA 2020 population), read from where each one says it is. Money that names no barangay is shown on its own. A project in two barangays counts in both, so barangays are never added up.

explore.guide.title: Guide
explore.guide.description: How to use the explorer, starter workbooks, and what the data holds.
explore.guide.start.ask: Type a question in the chat, like “health spending in 2027”. Your sheet changes to answer it, and Undo puts it back.
explore.guide.start.drag: Drag a breakdown, such as Office, from the list on the left onto Rows, or just click it. The chart draws at once.
explore.guide.start.starter: Open a finished workbook below and pick it apart. It replaces your workbook; Undo brings yours back.
explore.guide.starter.aip.name: Where the FY{year} AIP goes
explore.guide.starter.aip.blurb: The plan's estimated cost by office, by {goal} and by type of expense, side by side.
explore.guide.starter.climate.name: FY{year} climate change spending
explore.guide.starter.climate.blurb: Plan money tagged for adapting to and slowing climate change, by type and by office.
explore.guide.starter.income.name: Where the FY{year} money comes from
explore.guide.starter.income.blurb: The income the {lgu} expects, by class and its ten largest sources. Income is never added to spending.
explore.guide.starter.overTime.name: The budget over the years
explore.guide.starter.overTime.blurb: Every document on this site, one line each. Plans, proposals and enacted budgets are different money, so they are never added together.
explore.guide.howto.chart: Choose an amount for Columns and a breakdown for Rows. Marks, on the left, changes the kind of chart.
explore.guide.howto.compare: Tick more than one under Documents. They are shown side by side, never added together.
explore.guide.howto.filter: Press + after “where”, or drag a field onto Filters.
explore.guide.howto.drill: Click a bar, point or box (or a name in the Table view) to keep only it, leave it out, drill down to what is inside it, or list its records.
explore.guide.howto.recordsTitle: See the rows behind a chart.
explore.guide.howto.records: Records lists the programs, PPAs or account lines, 50 at a time. Click a column name to sort.
explore.guide.howto.board: New dashboard, at the bottom, shows up to four sheets. A click in one filters the others.
explore.guide.howto.share: Your workbook is saved in this browser only. Share makes a link that opens a copy for anyone, or downloads a picture or the figures.
explore.guide.key.enter: Add a field, open a menu, or open a name's menu in the Table view
explore.guide.key.esc: Close a menu or this guide
explore.guide.about.docsNote: A year can have up to three documents. They are steps of one budget, not three budgets.
explore.guide.about.money.aip: What a planned program is expected to cost if it is carried out. The plan lists more than the {lgu} can afford, so an estimated cost is not a budget and promises no money.
explore.guide.about.money.lep: What the {Mayor} asks the {council} to approve for next year, cut down from the plan to fit the income the {lgu} expects. It can still change.
explore.guide.about.money.ordinance: What the {council} passes into law. Only this lets the {lgu} spend, and only up to that amount. It is permission to spend, not a record of money spent.
explore.guide.about.never: Because these are different money, the explorer shows them side by side and never adds them together. Years are never added together either.
explore.guide.about.draft: A draft is a document the {lgu} has not published on this site yet. Drafts show only on test copies of the site, so the team can check them, and every draft figure carries a Draft label and stripes. Its figures may still change.
explore.guide.about.draftHere: This copy of the site shows drafts.
explore.guide.about.caveat.published: Only what the {lgu} has published is here. A year with nothing published is not listed.
explore.guide.about.caveat.lep: For some past years the {lgu} posted only the {Mayor}'s proposal (LEP), so those years have no enacted budget here.
explore.guide.about.caveat.themes: A program can have several themes or topics, so themes and topics do not add up to the total.
explore.guide.about.caveat.income: Income is the money the {lgu} expects to receive. It is never added to spending.
explore.guide.about.caveat.funds: Special funds, such as the 20% Development Fund and the disaster fund, are kinds of money, not offices. Find them under Fund.

explore.teach.starter: Or open a starter workbook and pick it apart:
explore.teach.empty: Nothing matches this sheet. Remove a filter above, or tick another document on the left.
explore.chat.forSheet: This chat belongs to “{sheet}”. Each sheet keeps its own.
